segments.speaker: ED
segments.en: Did you make notes while you were watching the performances of Romeo and Juliet, Gemma?

segments.speaker: GEMMA
segments.en: Yes, I did. I found it quite hard though. I kept getting too involved in the play.

segments.speaker: ED
segments.en: Me too. I ended up not taking notes. I wrote down my impressions when I got home. Do you mind if I check a few things with you? In case I've missed anything. And I’ve also got some questions about our assignment.

segments.speaker: GEMMA
segments.en: No, it’s good to talk things through. I may have missed things too.

segments.speaker: ED
segments.en: OK great. So first of all, I’m not sure how much information we should include in our reviews.

segments.speaker: GEMMA
segments.en: Right. Well, I don’t think we need to describe what happens. Especially as Romeo and Juliet is one of Shakespeare's most well-known plays.

segments.speaker: ED
segments.en: Yeah, everyone knows the story. In an essay we’d focus on the poetry and Shakespeare’s use of imagery etc., but that isn't really relevant in a review. We’re supposed to focus on how effective this particular production is.

segments.speaker: GEMMA
segments.en: Mmm. We should say what made it a success or a failure.

segments.speaker: ED
segments.en: And part of that means talking about the emotional impact the performance had /22 on us. I think that's important.

segments.speaker: GEMMA
segments.en: Yes. And we should definitely mention how well the director handled important /22 bits of the play - like when Romeo climbs onto Juliet’s balcony.

segments.speaker: ED
segments.en: And the fight between Mercutio and Tybalt.

segments.speaker: GEMMA
segments.en: Yes. It would also be interesting to mention the theatre space and how the director used it but I don’t think we’ll have space in 800 words.

segments.speaker: ED
segments.en: No. OK. That all sounds quite straightforward.

segments.speaker: ED
segments.en: So what about The Emporium Theatre’s production of the play?

segments.speaker: GEMMA
segments.en: I thought some things worked really well but there were some problems too.

segments.speaker: ED
segments.en: Yeah. What about the set, for example?

segments.speaker: GEMMA
segments.en: I think it was visually really stunning. I'd say that was probably the most memorable thing about this production.

segments.speaker: ED
segments.en: You’re right. The set design was really amazing, but actually I have seen similar ideas used in other productions.

segments.speaker: GEMMA
segments.en: What about the lighting? Some of the scenes were so dimly lit it was quite hard to see.

segments.speaker: ED
segments.en: I didn’t dislike it. It helped to change the mood of the quieter scenes.

segments.speaker: GEMMA
segments.en: That's a good point.

segments.speaker: ED
segments.en: What did you think of the costumes?

segments.speaker: GEMMA
segments.en: I was a bit surprised by the contemporary dress. I must say.

segments.speaker: ED
segments.en: Yeah - I think it worked well, but I had assumed it would be more conventional.

segments.speaker: GEMMA
segments.en: Me too. I liked the music at the beginning and I thought the musicians were brilliant, but I thought they were wasted because the music didn't have much impact in Acts 2 and 3.

segments.speaker: ED
segments.en: Yes - that was a shame.

segments.speaker: GEMMA
segments.en: One problem with this production was that the actors didn't deliver the lines that well. They were speaking too fast.

segments.speaker: ED
segments.en: It was a problem I agree, but I thought it was because they weren’t speaking loudly enough - especially at key points in the play.

segments.speaker: GEMMA
segments.en: I actually didn't have a problem with that.

segments.speaker: ED
segments.en: It’s been an interesting experience watching different versions of Romeo and Juliet, hasn’t it?

segments.speaker: GEMMA
segments.en: Definitely. It’s made me realise how relevant the play still is.

segments.speaker: ED
segments.en: Right. I mean a lot's changed since Shakespeare’s time, but in many ways nothing’s changed. There are always disagreements and tension between teenagers and their parents.

segments.speaker: GEMMA
segments.en: Yes, that's something all young people can relate to - more than the violence and the extreme emotions in the play.

segments.speaker: ED
segments.en: How did you find watching it in translation?

segments.speaker: GEMMA
segments.en: Really interesting. I expected to find it more challenging, but I could follow the story pretty well.

segments.speaker: ED
segments.en: I stopped worrying about not being able to understand all the words and focused on the actors’ expressions. The ending was pretty powerful. 029

segments.speaker: GEMMA
segments.en: Yes. That somehow intensified the emotion for me.

segments.speaker: ED
segments.en: Did you know Shakespeare’s been translated into more languages than any other writer?

segments.speaker: GEMMA
segments.en: What’s the reason for his international appeal, do you think?

segments.speaker: ED
segments.en: I was reading that it’s because his plays are about basic themes that people everywhere are familiar with.

segments.speaker: GEMMA
segments.en: Yeah, and they can also be understood on different levels. The characters have such depth.

segments.speaker: ED
segments.en: Right - which allows directors to experiment and find new angles.

segments.speaker: GEMMA
segments.en: That’s really important because ...

Questions 21-30
ROMEO AND JULIET REVIEW
Choose TWO letters A–E.

Text: Which TWO things do the students agree they need to include in their reviews of Romeo and Juliet?
Count: 2

    Id: A
    Text: analysis of the text
    Id: B
    Text: a summary of the plot
    Id: C
    Text: a description of the theatre
    Id: D
    Text: a personal reaction
    Id: E
    Text: a reference to particular scenes
Production aspects
Which opinion do the speakers give about each of the following aspects of The Emporium's production of Romeo and Juliet?
Choose FIVE answers from the box and write the correct letter A–G next to questions 23–27.

    Q Num: 23
    Text: The set
    Q Num: 24
    Text: The lighting

    Text: The costume design
    Q Num: 26
